transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-05 | Time: 11:00 AM PT | Duration: 45m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood CSM), Jonas (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Rachel (Helios Head of AI), Devon (Helios Platform), Priya (Helios Finance)

Summary: Quick QBR / health check covering usage, cost spikes in Feb, a couple of latency incidents at peak, and initial discussion about moving some workloads to Dedicated or Private to meet compliance and predictability needs.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we'll do a 45 minute QBR, quick health, then roadmap and next steps. Rachel, can you kick off with how things have been from your side?
[00:22] Rachel: Yeah thanks. Overall things are good, we hit about 2.2x growth in calls month-over-month. Biggest pain is cost — Feb had a couple of big spikes, unexpected. We saw a couple of slow responses too under heavy load which caused downstream retries.
[00:40] Maya: Got it, that's what we wanted to dig into. Jonas, Samir — we'll cover the numbers and then go into dedicated/private tradeoffs.
[00:52] Jonas: Quick note, thanks for the details you already shared in the sheet. On pricing — there are a few levers: batching, quantization profiles, and a Dedicated commitment option that gives predictable unit cost at scale.
[01:10] Priya: From finance perspective, the issue is the unpredictability. We budgeted for avg usage but those peaks blow the plan. How big a delta would Dedicated give us?
[01:25] Samir: Ballpark, customers with stable 24/7 throughput see 25–45% unit cost reduction when they move to Dedicated with the right batching and caching. But it depends on your token distribution, sequence length and KV cache hit rate.
[01:45] Devon: Quick clarifying q — when you say KV cache hit rate, is that our prefix/cache usage? We currently don't persist context across sessions; not sure our cache is configured.
[02:00] Samir: Right, happy to review your prefix patterns. If you can provide token distribution and session lengths we can estimate effective cache hit and savings.
[02:15] Rachel: We can share that. Also, a reliability question — we had two slowdowns around 2/18 and 2/23, were those infra incidents or model throttling?
[02:29] Maya: We looked into those. Samir, do you want to summarize root cause?
[02:34] Samir: Sure. There were simultaneous large-batch spikes from a few customers in the same region, combined with a cache warm-up on longer sequences — the runtime routed to a fallback variant for a minute which added latency. Also a minor autoscale lag during a central region deployment. Not a data loss incident but extra latency.
[02:56] Devon: Was that the KV cash warm-up? I keep seeing 'cash' in the logs — transcription aside — but yes it sounds like cache warm-up.
[03:08] Maya: (laughs) transcription quirk. The action here is to run a canary for warm starts and add pre-warm caching for your main routes.
[03:20] Rachel: That would help. What about observability — we want per-route latency and token-level cost breakdowns. The console has that but it's a lot to parse. Can Redwood provide a rolling dashboard or a CSV export?
[03:36] Jonas: Yes, we can export per-route granularity and we can set up a dashboard with the metrics you want. Also we'll share a cost-by-route worksheet for you to play with scenarios (batching on/off, quant profile).
[03:52] Priya: That worksheet will be important. Also audit/compliance — SOC 2 + KMS are prerequisites for internal approval. Where are we on those docs?
[04:04] Maya: We have SOC 2 Type II and KMS integration docs ready. I'll re-share the security pack and a pointer to the private deployment whitepaper. Jonas will coordinate legal if you want an NDA or SSO details.
[04:18] Jonas: Yep I'll be the contact for legal/security. We can also coordinate a short session with our infra/security engineer.
[04:28] Rachel: On Private — we have some regulated models and need VPC + customer-managed KMS. What are the rough lead times and cost differences vs Dedicated?
[04:39] Samir: Private (VPC/on-prem) has more setup time — typically 6–12 weeks depending on networking and audit needs. Dedicated pools are faster — usually days to provision after commit. Cost delta depends: Private has infra pass-through and a platform fee; Dedicated is a managed reserved capacity which can be cheaper overall if you don't have heavy networking/security customizations.
[05:02] Devon: For us, the deciding factor is data residency and having control over audit logs. Can Private give us full raw audit logs and key control?
[05:12] Maya: Yes — Private supports customer-managed KMS and raw audit logs with retention controls. We'll put together a matrix of features per deployment type.
[05:24] Rachel: Great. Also, can Redwood help with model/regression monitoring? We saw some drift in generation quality after a prompt pattern changed.
[05:33] Samir: We have Redwood Optimize and eval hooks — you can anchor prompt sets and get quality regression alerts tied to specific prompt sets. We can run a diff on the time windows you saw drift.
[05:46] Rachel: Let's do that; I can send a small eval set.
[05:50] Maya: Action: Samir will run a benchmark on your sample set and share latency/cost numbers. Samir, anything you need from them?
[05:58] Samir: I need a representative sample (500–1k requests), the token lengths and whether you use streaming or full responses. Also the model config you are using in prod.
[06:11] Devon: We'll export the traffic slice.
[06:14] Priya: Back to the cost question — what immediate changes could drop our Feb costs quickly?
[06:21] Samir: Short term: enable prefix caching, tune batch sizes, switch to a lower quant profile for non-critical routes, and offload embeddings to a cheaper model where acceptable. Those typically give the fastest wins.
[06:35] Rachel: Could we see an estimate of savings if we toggled those?
[06:39] Jonas: We'll run scenario modeling in the worksheet and include projected monthly spend under current vs optimized vs Dedicated.
[06:47] Maya: I'm going to propose a phased plan: 1) short-term ops wins (cache + batching tweaks) 2) benchmark to quantify 3) decision on Dedicated vs Private based on cost + compliance 4) if Private chosen, schedule network deep-dive. Does that align?
[07:02] Rachel: Sounds good. Priya — are you ok with that timeline?
[07:07] Priya: Yes but finance needs the hardened numbers for Q2 budget. The worksheet must include conservative/worst-case scenarios.
[07:15] Maya: We'll provide low/med/high spend projections.
[07:19] Jonas: On procurement, if you go Dedicated we'll need an MSA + capacity commitment. I can send the draft commitment ranges.
[07:27] Priya: Please do.
[07:30] Rachel: A couple other items — latency SLOs. Can Redwood offer SLOing per route? We need 95th percentile under 300ms for our interactive route.
[07:40] Samir: We can set per-route SLOs and add tracing hooks. For the 300ms target we might need to pin a lower-latency model variant and configure autoscale. We'll verify in the benchmark.
[07:52] Devon: For Private, any special IP allowlist or transit gateway requirements we should plan for?
[08:00] Samir: Usually customers plan for an IP allowlist + a peering/transit gateway. We'll share a network checklist.
[08:08] Maya: Ok let's call out owners and dates. Action items will be in the doc I'll send after.
[08:14] Rachel: Quick question — any mention of competitors? We briefly POC'ed Anthropic but they didn't have the same Dedicated tooling.
[08:22] Jonas: Noted. We also compared to OpenAI for managed endpoints; Redwood's differentiation is the Dedicated + Private path and observability.
[08:32] Priya: Final note on security — we will need SSO (SAML) and RBAC before we open access to non-dev teams.
[08:40] Maya: We support SAML and granular RBAC; I'll include setup steps.
[08:44] Rachel: Great. Anything else from Redwood side?
[08:48] Jonas: I'll coordinate legal and send the Dedicated commit ranges.
[08:51] Samir: I'll start the benchmark as soon as we get the sample.
[08:55] Devon: We'll share the traffic profile and token distribution by 2026-03-09.
[09:01] Priya: Finance will review the worksheet and give feedback.
[09:05] Maya: Thanks everyone. I'll send the QBR deck, the security pack and the cost worksheet within 48 hours. We'll follow up on the deep-dive week of 2026-03-16.
[09:20] Rachel: Thanks all, that was helpful.

Recap / Next steps (brief):
- Maya to send Q2 pricing, security pack, and cost-by-route worksheet (within 48h)
- Samir to run latency/cost benchmarks on Helios sample (by 2026-03-11)
- Devon to provide traffic profile and token distribution (by 2026-03-09)
- Jonas to coordinate legal/SOC2 docs handoff and schedule private deployment deep-dive (target wk of 2026-03-16)

End of transcript.
